name: Binary Analysis & Reverse Engineering
description: Disassembly, decompilation, binary similarity, and reverse engineering of compiled code.
narrative:
The earliest papers in this list, clustered in 2018, show binary analysis grappling with the foundational problem that compiled code throws away almost everything useful: symbols, types, structure, and even reliable instruction boundaries. Work like "Debin: Predicting Debug Information in Stripped Binaries" (CCS 2018) and "Using Logic Programming to Recover C++ Classes and Methods from Compiled Executables" (CCS 2018) tried to recover lost high-level information, while "Superset Disassembly: Statically Rewriting x86 Binaries Without Heuristics" (NDSS 2018) attacked the equally stubborn problem of just disassembling and rewriting x86 reliably. A parallel security-application thread appears in the same year — turning analysis into offense and defense, as in "Block Oriented Programming: Automating Data-Only Attacks" (CCS 2018) and the malware-focused unpacking and de-virtualization work like "VMHunt" (CCS 2018) and the Android unpacker study (NDSS 2018).

The clear breakthrough shift is the arrival of machine learning for binary representation. "Asm2Vec" (S&P 2019) was a watershed, showing that learned embeddings of assembly could survive obfuscation and compiler-optimization noise for clone search, and it triggered a wave: "DeepBinDiff" (NDSS 2020) for program-wide diffing and "PalmTree: Learning an Assembly Language Model for Instruction Embedding" (CCS 2021), which brought BERT-style pretraining to instructions. By 2022 the field paused to take stock with "How Machine Learning Is Solving the Binary Function Similarity Problem" (USENIX 2022), a sobering measurement study of what actually works.

Alongside the learning revolution, the systems-and-tooling side matured. "RetroWrite: Statically Instrumenting COTS Binaries for Fuzzing and Sanitization" (S&P 2020) and "Breaking Through Binaries" (USENIX 2021) pushed compiler-quality instrumentation into binary-only fuzzing, while "SymQEMU" (NDSS 2021) made symbolic execution practical on raw binaries. The community also consolidated hard-won knowledge in "SoK: All You Ever Wanted to Know About x86/x64 Binary Disassembly But Were Afraid to Ask" (S&P 2021) and even studied the humans doing the work in "RE-Mind: a First Look Inside the Mind of a Reverse Engineer" (USENIX 2022). A strong embedded/firmware vertical grew here too, from "FirmXRay" (CCS 2020) through "BaseSpec" (NDSS 2021) and "FirmWire" (NDSS 2022) for cellular basebands.

Where it stands now is a convergence of probabilistic recovery and large language models. Probabilistic structure recovery in "OSPREY" (S&P 2021) set the stage for LLM-driven approaches that now dominate the recovery problem: "DeGPT: Optimizing Decompiler Output with LLM" (NDSS 2024) and "ReSym: Harnessing LLMs to Recover Variable and Data Structure Symbols from Stripped Binaries" (CCS 2024) use LLMs to clean up decompiler output and recover symbols, while similarity research keeps refining its representations, as in "Code is not Natural Language" (USENIX 2024), which argues for semantics-oriented graphs over treating assembly as text. The throughline is consistent: recover what the compiler erased — boundaries, symbols, types, structure, and semantics — increasingly with learned and now LLM-based models, while building the rewriting and instrumentation plumbing that lets those analyses run on real-world stripped binaries.

milestones.title: Superset Disassembly: Statically Rewriting x86 Binaries Without Heuristics
milestones.note: tackled reliable static rewriting of x86 without fragile heuristics, a foundation for binary-only instrumentation

milestones.title: Asm2Vec: Boosting Static Representation Robustness for Binary Clone Search against Code Obfuscation and Compiler Optimization
milestones.note: watershed that showed learned assembly embeddings could survive obfuscation and optimization, igniting the ML-for-binaries wave

milestones.title: RetroWrite: Statically Instrumenting COTS Binaries for Fuzzing and Sanitization
milestones.note: brought near-compiler-quality static instrumentation to closed-source binaries for fuzzing and sanitization

milestones.title: PalmTree: Learning an Assembly Language Model for Instruction Embedding
milestones.note: applied language-model pretraining to instructions, producing reusable embeddings across binary analysis tasks

milestones.title: SoK: All You Ever Wanted to Know About x86/x64 Binary Disassembly But Were Afraid to Ask
milestones.note: consolidated decades of disassembly knowledge and benchmarked the field's hardest core problem

milestones.title: How Machine Learning Is Solving the Binary Function Similarity Problem
milestones.note: rigorous measurement study that grounded the hype around ML-based binary similarity in reproducible evidence

milestones.title: DeGPT: Optimizing Decompiler Output with LLM
milestones.note: marked the LLM turn by using large language models to improve decompiler output for reverse engineers

milestones.title: ReSym: Harnessing LLMs to Recover Variable and Data Structure Symbols from Stripped Binaries
milestones.note: showed LLMs recovering variable and data-structure symbols, pushing decompilation toward source-level fidelity
